$comment: Worked example. Every value here is verified against a real stock 4.8.117 bundle -- use it as the schema reference for new versions.
$electron_version_source: Contents/Frameworks/Electron Framework.framework/Resources/Info.plist -> CFBundleVersion. NOTE: CFBundleShortVersionString is absent from that plist; read CFBundleVersion. Must match the fetched runtime EXACTLY -- the .node modules are Nan-built, so the ABI is not stable across Electron majors.

patches.why: hp_configs.crashAutoSubmit stays true otherwise, and crash dumps auto-upload to http://15.23.17.24:9100 in plaintext. A previous attempt set a TOP-LEVEL key of the same name, which the code never reads -- crash-reporter.js reads packagejson.hp_configs.crashAutoSubmit.

Squirrel otherwise downloads HP's x86_64 build and offers to replace ours. This early return is the real gate: Squirrel.Mac does NOT version-compare client-side, so bumping package.json version does not stop it. Reached via main.js -> app-starter.js -> require('./app-updater').

PRE-EXISTING HP BUG, present on Intel too. index.html loads this as a classic <script src>, where top-level `export` is a syntax error; the main process gets away with require()ing it only because Node 22+ can require an ES module. Converting to CommonJS satisfies both consumers. Stock build logs 'Uncaught SyntaxError: Unexpected token export'; patched build logs zero.

$do_not_patch.app/shared/shared.module.js: Dead code -- the live copy is webpacked into bundle.js. An earlier pass half-converted it (rewrote the export, left a top-level import), which is pure noise. Leave it alone.
$do_not_patch.app/machan.js: Dead code -- 242 concatenated module bodies with colliding const declarations; cannot load as a single CommonJS module.

required_dylibs.name: libidn2.0.dylib
required_dylibs.why: The arm64 slice of Dj{Core,Conn}ServicesNative-Electron.node has flat-namespace undefined symbols _idn2_check_version, _idn2_free, _idn2_lookup_ul, _idn2_strerror and ZERO libidn2 load commands. The x86_64 slice has none of them. HP's arm64 build links a curl with IDN support and never ships the library. Flat lookup resolves at CALL time, so the app launches fine and only dies on IDN code paths -- do not conclude from a clean launch that this is unnecessary.

required_dylibs.name: libnghttp2.14.dylib
required_dylibs.why: The arm64 slice of Dj{Core,Conn}ServicesNative-Electron.node has 36 flat-namespace undefined _nghttp2_* symbols from HP's libcurl build with HTTP/2 support. Same class as the idn2 gap: HP links a curl with h2 and ships no nghttp2. nghttp2 is MIT licensed.  NOTE: the formula is libnghttp2, NOT nghttp2. Homebrew split the library out into its own formula; the nghttp2 bottle now contains the command-line tools and no .dylib at all, so fetching it downloads and verifies fine and then finds nothing to extract.
required_dylibs.$measured: ALPN measured 2026-07-31: us1.api.ws-hp.com negotiates http/1.1 ONLY -- an earlier note wrongly cited it as an h2 endpoint. lfp-downloads.hpcloud.hp.com DOES negotiate h2, but that is the updater host, which this patch disables. So no confirmed h2 path is exercised by the patched build today. Bundled anyway because the cost is one small MIT dylib and the failure mode is a hard process abort at call time on any HP endpoint that later enables h2.
required_dylibs.$preload_note: MUST be true. These symbols are flat-namespace ('dynamically looked up'), which dyld resolves only against images ACTUALLY LOADED in the process. Nothing declares a load command for libnghttp2, so with preload:false the dylib sits in the bundle, satisfies an `nm -gU` scan, and is never loaded -- verified with vmmap: libidn2/libunistring/libintl LOADED, libnghttp2 NOT LOADED. Presence on disk is not satisfaction.

$not_a_dependency.libmagic.1.dylib: HP already ships this, already universal (x86_64 arm64). Linked by both .node modules, JDFPrintProcessor and goyaApp. Do not copy or replace it.

$unresolved_symbols_note._png_init_filter_functions_neon: RESOLVED 2026-08-27. This fired: importing PNGs crashed the app with EXC_BAD_ACCESS, PC=0x0, LR inside DjCoreServicesNative -- a call through a null pointer. The earlier note called it an accepted, unverified risk and warned that a call site existed; it did. The build now compiles clickgraft/shims/pngshim.c and preloads it, which supplies the symbol as a no-op. That is correct rather than a workaround: libpng installs its portable C filter implementations first and calls this only to override them with NEON versions, so nothing is lost that this build ever had.

$expected_x86_only_note: Orphaned: nothing in the bundle links it and it is not mapped into any running process. The live APPE path uses AdobeAXE8SharedExpat, which is universal. Leave it; just do not let verify fail on it.
verified_by: Long-supported. Rebuilt 2026-08-27 with the libpng shim after the null-call crash was found; verified. Its print path has been exercised since the project began.
$accepted_unprovided_symbols_note: Carbon Multiprocessing Services, removed from macOS long ago. Referenced by AdobePDFL, libACR, libACRstd, JDFPrintProcessor and DjCoreServicesNative -- Adobe's RIP stack. ACCEPTED, not shimmed: unlike png_init_filter_functions_neon, where a no-op is the correct behaviour because libpng installs C fallbacks first, these return values a caller acts on (a task id, per-task storage). A plausible-looking lie could cause subtly wrong rendering instead of an honest crash. They are equally unresolvable in HP's own x86_64 build, so Adobe's code has evidently guarded these paths for years. Revisit if a crash ever lands with PC=0 and LR inside the Adobe stack.
